extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, editors, bibliographers, and readers of yearbook/indexes of short stories
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and metrics for identifying, classifying, and indexing 'distinctive' short stories published in American periodicals over a defined year, plus magazine-level statistics and inclusion/exclusion rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk distinction system
rubrics_metrics.description: One, two, or three asterisks are prefixed to the titles of stories to indicate distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one, two, or three asterisks to mark relative distinction. Three-asterisk stories are singled out as highest distinction (see separate entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-asterisk stories (permanent literary value / Rolls of Honor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-asterisk stories are of somewhat permanent literary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-asterisk stories 'entitle' the story to a place on the annual 'Rolls of Honor.' They indicate a higher category of lasting literary worth compared with one- or two-asterisk stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/exclusion of reprints and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The list excludes reprints but not translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When counting or indexing 'distinctive' stories, omit reprinted items from consideration; treat translations as eligible and include them in counts and rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time scope for inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The period under consideration is October, 1920, to September, 1921, inclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only stories published within the defined Oct. 1920–Sep. 1921 window are indexed in the main listing; a small number of distinctive stories published between Oct. 1919 and Sep. 1920 are included if they could not be read in the previous year and were specially considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazine-level metrics (counts and percentages)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each periodical the table includes: No. of stories published, No. of distinctive stories published, Percentage of distinctive stories published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these three metrics to evaluate a periodical's output of distinctive short fiction. The tables also break out counts by single (*), double (**), and triple (***) asterisk categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking criteria for periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodicals are ranked both by percentage of distinctive stories and by number of distinctive stories published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide separate ranked lists (e.g., by percentage and by absolute number). When ties occur, decide them 'by taking relative rank in other lists into account' (i.e., use secondary ranking lists as tiebreakers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing scope by title/magazine
rubrics_metrics.description: All short stories published in a specified list of magazines and newspapers are indexed; only 'stories of distinction' are indexed for other listed magazines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page enumerates which periodicals are fully indexed (e.g., All's Well, Atlantic Monthly, Harper's Magazine, Scribner's, Saturday Evening Post, etc.) and which are indexed only for stories of distinction or special attention (a secondary list). Follow the specified magazine inclusion rules when compiling the index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-inclusion rule for stories called specially to attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain stories of distinction published in other magazines are indexed because they have been specially called to the author's attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow exceptions to regular indexing scope for notable items brought to attention; note such provenance in the index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references and citation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross references after an author's name refer to previous volumes of the series; the figures in parentheses after a title refer to the volume and page number of the magazine (or page number only where pagination is discontinuous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these citation conventions consistently in the index. Abbreviations for periodicals are standardized (list provided); use them when space requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prefixed letters to indicate prior representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodicals represented in the lists during 1915, 1916, 1917, 1918, 1919, and 1920 are represented by the prefixed letters a, b, c, d, e, and f respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When listing periodicals across multiple years, prefix with the indicated letters to show historical representation on the lists.
